securityAchievement.securityAchievementDescription: NovaCivic notifies FedRAMP of significant changes to FGC via fedramp@novacivic.com and the FedRAMP portal per the Significant Change Notification process defined in SCN-001.
fedramp@novacivic.com is hosted on a dedicated mail domain with explicit allow-listing for @fedramp.gov and @gsa.gov to prevent filtering by anti-spam controls.
fedramp@novacivic.com is hosted on Fastmail's dedicated government-compatible mail infrastructure with a 99.9% uptime SLA, independent of the primary novacivic.com mail domain.
FedRAMP required actions received at fedramp@novacivic.com are assigned to an owner in the NovaCivic security ticket system within 4 hours and tracked to completion within stated deadlines.
Emergency messages received at fedramp@novacivic.com trigger an immediate PagerDuty alert to the on-call Security Operations engineer, ensuring 24/7 coverage within the 4-hour SLA.
Important messages from FedRAMP are logged as tickets in the NovaCivic security issue tracker and assigned to the appropriate team within 1 business day.
NovaCivic acknowledges all FedRAMP communications within 4 hours for Emergency messages and 1 business day for all other message types.

FGC production systems are scanned by Qualys VMDR on a continuous basis. AWS GuardDuty provides continuous threat detection across all in-scope AWS accounts. Critical findings are triaged within 24 hours.

securityAchievement.securityAchievementDescription: The FGC Ongoing Certification Report (OCR) is published quarterly to the NovaCivic trust center at trust.novacivic.com and made available to all authorized agency customers.
Each FGC Ongoing Certification Report includes the scheduled date of the next report in the document header. The next report is scheduled for 2026-09-01.
The FGC trust center includes a secure feedback form at trust.novacivic.com/feedback for authorized agency customers to submit questions, concerns, or comments about the OCR.
Anonymized feedback summaries from agency customers are included in the following quarter's OCR, with specific agency identifiers removed to protect confidentiality.
FGC OCRs published to the public trust center are reviewed by the CISO before publication to confirm no sensitive security details, vulnerability specifics, or PII are included.

FGC OCRs are published to the public-facing trust center. OCRs are cleared for public release by CISO review. Sensitive assessment details are retained in the authenticated portion of the trust center.
NovaCivic conducts a quarterly review meeting open to all authorized agency customers using FGC. Meeting invitations and agenda are distributed 30 days in advance via the trust center and email.
Quarterly review meeting registration information, including video conference link and agenda, is published to trust.novacivic.com at least 30 days before each meeting.
Each quarterly review meeting concludes with announcement of the date and registration link for the following quarter's meeting, also posted to the trust center.

Quarterly review materials and recordings do not include specific vulnerability details, unmitigated findings, or other information that could assist adversaries. Content is reviewed by CISO before publication.
FGC quarterly review meetings include a roadmap update, security posture summary, recent OCR walkthrough, and an open Q&A session for agency customers.
All FGC quarterly review meetings are recorded and transcribed. Recordings and transcripts are published to the authenticated portion of the trust center within 5 business days.
FGC quarterly review recordings and transcripts are restricted to authorized agency customers. Third parties not serving a current agency customer are not granted access without CISO approval.
NovaCivic shares quarterly review recordings responsibly, restricting distribution to authenticated agency portal users. Recordings are not posted to public-facing platforms.
All quarterly review content, including slides and transcripts, is reviewed by CISO before distribution to confirm no sensitive security information is included.
FGC public certification information including service description, authorization status, authorization path, UEI, trust center URL, and primary contacts is maintained at trust.novacivic.com.
The NovaCivic trust center maintains a current list of all services included under the FGC FedRAMP certification: FGC Core, FGC Financial Reporting, and FGC Analytics.
All FedRAMP certification materials for FGC are hosted at trust.novacivic.com, a FedRAMP-compatible trust center providing both public and authenticated agency access to certification data.

FGC certification data is published in both human-readable format on the trust center web UI and machine-readable JSON via the trust center API. Both formats are updated simultaneously at publication.

NovaCivic shares FGC certification information responsibly. Sensitive assessment details and vulnerability specifics are restricted to the authenticated agency portal. Public-facing data contains only non-sensitive certification metadata.
Historical FGC OCRs and quarterly review materials are retained in the trust center for a minimum of 3 years and remain accessible to authorized agency customers.

The FGC Minimum Assessment Scope includes all AWS GovCloud infrastructure, ECS Fargate tasks, Aurora PostgreSQL databases, S3 storage, ALB, WAF, GuardDuty, Config, and the Okta Government Cloud identity tenant.
FGC processes grant management data at the Moderate impact level. Data flows are documented in the FGC System Description, including grant applicant PII, award financials, and performance reports.
AWS GovCloud (FedRAMP High authorized, FR2020-000001) and Okta Government Cloud are the primary third-party information resources within the FGC assessment boundary. Both are documented in the COP.
All FGC information resources in the asset inventory include metadata fields for system name, owner, data classification, impact level, and last-reviewed date per the FGC Asset Tagging Policy.
Supplemental scope information including agency tenant isolation architecture, data flow diagrams, and network topology is maintained in the authenticated section of the NovaCivic trust center.
The FGC Secure Configuration Guide (SCG) documents recommended configurations for Okta SSO integration, agency tenant RBAC setup, MFA policy enforcement, and audit log forwarding to agency SIEM.
The FGC SCG includes step-by-step instructions for applying each recommended configuration, including screen-by-screen guidance for Okta tenant setup and FGC administrative console settings.
The FGC SCG is publicly available at docs.novacivic.com/security/scg without authentication, enabling agencies to review recommended configurations before and during onboarding.
FGC is configured with secure defaults: FIDO2 MFA is enforced by default, TLS 1.2+ is required, and audit logging is enabled on all agency tenants. Administrators cannot disable these settings.
All FGC significant changes are logged in the GitHub repository commit history and recorded in a change management register maintained in Jira with classification, risk assessment, and approvals.

FGC change notifications include change description, change classification, risk assessment, deployment date, rollback plan, and affected services as required by the FedRAMP Significant Change Notification rules.
Historical FGC significant change notifications are retained for 3 years and available in both the Jira change register and the authenticated section of the trust center.
FGC change notifications are published in human-readable format on the trust center and in machine-readable JSON via the trust center API for programmatic consumption by agency customers.
Significant FGC changes are communicated to FedRAMP via the FedRAMP portal and to agency customers via trust center notifications and email to registered agency security contacts.
All FGC changes are evaluated for potential security impact using the Change Classification Matrix in CMP-001 Appendix A before deployment. Changes classified as Transformative require CISO approval.
Emergency changes to FGC are deployed immediately with CISO verbal approval and documented retroactively within 24 hours. FedRAMP and affected agencies are notified within 4 hours of deployment.
Adaptive changes to FGC are communicated to FedRAMP and agency customers via the trust center notification feed no later than 30 days after deployment.

All FGC security events are evaluated against the FedRAMP PAIN rating matrix within 2 hours of detection to determine FedRAMP reportability. Triage is performed by Security Operations using IRP-001 guidance.

When full incident impact cannot be determined within 2 hours, NovaCivic defaults to PAIN rating Medium and immediately notifies FedRAMP with available information, updating the rating as investigation progresses.

Federal impact is estimated based on the number of affected agency tenants, data categories involved, and duration of exposure, using the FGC Incident Impact Estimation Worksheet in IRP-001 Appendix B.
FGC submits automated initial incident reports to FedRAMP via the FedRAMP API within 1 hour of determining FedRAMP reportability, using a structured JSON payload defined in IRP-001.

FGC uses AWS KMS (FIPS 140-2 Level 2 validated) for all data at-rest encryption and TLS 1.2+ for all data in-transit. Cryptographic module documentation is maintained in the FGC System Description and updated annually.
Each agency tenant's data is encrypted with a dedicated AWS KMS key. Key policies prevent cross-tenant access. Agency administrators cannot access or modify encryption keys for other tenants.

FGC is designed for federal grant-making agencies at the CFO Act agency level administering competitive and formula grants. Intended use cases include award management, SF-425 reporting, and grants portfolio analytics.

NovaCivic is actively pursuing FedRAMP 20x certification for FGC. The independent assessment was completed by ClearPath Federal Assessment Services, LLC in Q1 2026. FGC is in the final FedRAMP review phase.
NovaCivic has submitted a FedRAMP marketplace listing request for FGC. The listing includes authorized agency use cases, service description, trust center link, and contact information.
The FGC FedRAMP certification package consists of this SDR and the associated Certification Overview Package (COP), both maintained in the NovaCivic trust center and the FedRAMP portal.
The FGC COP and SDR are authored and maintained in conformance with the FedRAMP JSON schemas for cr26CertificationOverviewPackage and cr26SecurityDecisionRecord.

NovaCivic maintains full responsibility and accountability for all FGC security controls, including those partially implemented in leveraged FedRAMP-authorized services such as AWS GovCloud and Okta Government Cloud.

NovaCivic applied for FedRAMP 20x certification through the marketplace listing process per FRC-APP-AFC. The application was submitted on 2026-01-07 following completion of the independent assessment.
This SDR constitutes the FGC initial implementation summaries, covering all applicable KSIs and FRR requirements for a FedRAMP 20x Class A certification.

NovaCivic addresses all applicable FedRAMP rules for Class A certification as documented in this SDR. Class A evidence is primarily attestation-based with manual validation, appropriate to the service's risk profile.
